Almost everybody likes a good joke, but they also appreciate a good read and discussion.

So I was wondering if it was at all feasible to have separate comment sections so comments don't get cluttered with jokes at the top while people looking for serious info have to stroll through the whole comment section to have great comments sitting on low scores as most people don't bother going through a whole thread upvoating good content.

I doubt if this will work or solve anything, just a thought.

Edit: Thanks for the replies, I can see how this is so not gonna work, upvoats for all participants. :)
Have an entertainment and serious discussion section in comments?

Having entirely seperate sections would be a bit too much, but perhaps a way to mark your comment as serious and then an option to filter out any non-serious comments would work. That way people who want to see all comments wouldn't need to go to two different sections.

Why not just let the votes decide? If it's a serious topic, the serious responses should be voted to the top. If it's a funny post or lighthearted, there may be more allowance for "I did nazi that coming" puns and other drivel.

Downvoting should be used when a comment does not contribute to discussion. Whether a comment contributes to discussion should be based on the topic or seriousness of discussion.

One question. How would you stop people from clicking to make a serious comment and then making jokes?

You could report it to a mod but who has the time? As Voat grows the amount of comments that are "in the wrong section" would go up and up, and that's not taking into account that's there's no objective way to decide whether something is serious or not. Someone might well like to mix in humour with seriousness, to break up the monologue and keep it interesting. This way doesn't allow for any grey areas, or take into account that people's opinions on what is and isn't serious can be quite varied, or misled, for example someone making a joke that doesn't read well as one. I think it's better the way it is.

Long term this may be a good idea, but for right now there's not enough content to filter like that.

I'm also hoping that Voat survives for some time before becoming as circle-jerky as Reddit.

For those who don't know, Extra Life is a charitable organization tied in with the Children's Miracle Network. They raise money to help sick kids in children's hospitals around the US (and the world).

Participants play games for 24 hours. In a row. It started out with video games but the last three years have seen an explosion of table top games. You ask friends, family members and what have you to sponsor you and then you game your face off over one full day.

This will be my fourth year doing it - I and my team have raised over $10k in that time, picked up some publisher sponsorship and it gives me one day a year where I know all of my family and friends will be together, chucking dice and drawing cards.

This year's game day is November 7th - but you can do an event any time.
